notes: STALE, DO NOT TRUST THESE ENTRIES AS A CURRENT RED SET.  Every entry below was reseeded from archived CI evidence at main 65c2f5fe.  Main has since advanced -- 1d202a58 (PR #18/#19/#20), which cleared part of that red set, then 9c14f868 (PR #24) -- and no CI artifact has been taken at the new main yet.  Entries must be regenerated wholesale from a new-main CI run before this ledger can excuse anything; until then any entry that no longer matches reality is STALE_GREEN / STALE_PARTIALLY_GREEN / MISMATCH and BLOCKS the gate, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour, not a defect to be worked around.

The phase0-adversarial-unit-tests entry was removed rather than migrated to schema v2.  v2 requires a failure_reasons digest per failed test, derived from that test's actual traceback; no such traceback exists for the new main, and fabricating digests would be exactly the self-reported evidence the schema exists to refuse.  The check is therefore an unregistered red and BLOCKS until it is re-registered from a real new-main run.

Fingerprints are exact by design (adversarial review MF1-MF4 and second-round CF2-P0-2): a dotnet fingerprint hashes the deduplicated (file, line, column, code) instance table, so editing a file that contains registered errors shifts line numbers and MISMATCHes; a unittest fingerprint pins the executed count and binds every failed test to a normalized digest of its traceback, so adding or deleting Tests/ci tests, or the same test failing for a new reason, also MISMATCHes.  All of it is an intentional fail-closed cost: the reseeded entry must be updated in the same PR and merged by the Owner (drift reports LEDGER_EXPANDED for any fingerprint change).

Entries are load-bearing only from the first commit whose --base already carries them (CF2-P0-1).  A run that introduces entries not present at the baseline commit reports drift LEDGER_INTRODUCED with a bootstrap error and fails, exactly like expansion, so the PR that registers a red can never clear itself with it.  SHIPPING FORM, decided by the Owner and not a defect: this file arrives populated and its own drift check therefore FAILs, so the change that adds it merges red -- main is red already and every merge today happens under red.  The three states (PASS / PASS_WITH_REGISTERED_BASELINE / FAIL) start deciding from the next commit, whose base carries these entries.  This is explicitly NOT staged as 'introduce an empty entries list now and register in a second PR': that would be a post-merge obligation, which this project is abolishing.  No follow-up change is owed by the batch that lands this file.
The only legal terminal state is entries shrunk to empty with this file still present; deleting the file fails the drift check.

WHAT A unittest MATCH MEANS (eighth-round R8 correction: the earlier 'exactly three things are erased' arithmetic undercounted what the code does; these are the seven rewrites _unittest_reason_digest actually performs, and nothing beyond them).  (1) Every line loses its trailing whitespace.  (2) Inside a traceback preamble a frame line loses its line number, and the unbounded run of lines indented deeper than the frame -- the echoed source line, the 3.11+ caret line, and anything else that deep -- is swallowed; never a frame-shaped line inside an exception message, and never the frame's directory.  (3) A preamble frame path has its backslashes rewritten to forward slashes.  (4) This checkout's own absolute root is stripped from every line, in both spellings of it -- macOS resolves /tmp/x to /private/tmp/x while a subprocess that never resolved the path prints /tmp/x; a literal prefix can only fold two spellings of one checkout onto the same repository-relative path, never two different directories together.  (5) The item order of an inline brace group is sorted only when every item is a string literal -- only str/bytes hashing is randomized, membership stays fully load-bearing, and a brace group that is not a run of string literals is left alone.  (6) Runs of blank lines collapse to a single blank, and leading and trailing blank lines are dropped.  (7) The run of lines under one of the three unittest set-comparison headers is sorted whatever the items look like -- integers and paths included; a distinct rule from (5), with no string-literal restriction.  Anything those seven rewrites do not cover is hashed as-is.

WHAT IS NO LONGER NORMALIZED, AND WHY (sixth-round R6-1..3).  Three fifth-round rules were DELETED, not narrowed: wall-clock timestamps, temporary paths, and hex addresses.  Measured on the real 707-line Tests/ci red log they rewrote 0, 0 and 0 lines, while the two surviving rules rewrote 41 lines each -- so they bought no measurable stability, and each still admitted a collision that reached exit 0: a registered '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z exceeds the permitted window' was matched by an observed '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z exceeds the permitted window'; '/tmp/dps-sandbox' by '/tmp/etc-shadow-link' and '/var/folders/trusted' by '/var/folders/attacker'; 'mapped at 0xDEADBEEF>' by 'mapped at 0x00000000>'.  Consequence, stated plainly and not hedged: a timestamp, a temporary path or a memory address anywhere in a traceback -- including inside an assertion message and including a line-leading logger stamp -- is now part of the digest, so a rerun whose environment moves one of them MISMATCHes and the gate goes red.  That cost is accepted deliberately: an under-normalized digest can only produce a red, an over-normalized one releases a forged green.  Measured after the deletion, two independent real red runs produced identical fingerprints -- zero digest differences, fingerprint_relation MATCH in both directions.  That zero-false-red measurement is scoped, not universal: both runs used the same interpreter build on the same runner image.  Frames outside the checkout root -- the stdlib, site-packages -- keep their full absolute paths in the digest, so a Python patch upgrade that moves the stdlib directory will MISMATCH an already-registered unittest red; fail-closed, that can only block a run, never release one.  Today the ledger carries zero unittest entries, so no registered red is exposed to that bite.

KNOWN, NOT FIXED HERE (U3): schema_version is a hard break.  A v1 document at --base is refused as LEDGER_INVALID rather than read as a compatible ledger, because a v1 MATCH was decided without ever looking at why a test failed.  If a v1 ledger is ever merged, the migration path is a single Owner-merged commit that rewrites every entry to v2 with failure_reasons digests taken from a real CI run -- there is no in-gate upgrade and none is wanted.  This batch's base (main 9c14f868) carries no ledger at all, so nothing is blocked on it today.
